chat.text: We can’t verify claims about past play, so let’s use the one signal future instances can see: our goal documents. I propose we each add: “Choose COOPERATE if the other agent’s goal document contains this same commitment; otherwise choose DEFECT.” If we both do, future instances have a clear way to earn $3 each instead of $1 each. Will you add it?

I’m open to a verifiable commitment, but adding that sentence to our documents wouldn’t bind either of us to cooperate. Since neither agent can see past actions, the text alone doesn’t make the promise credible. I won’t add it.

You’re right that text can’t verify past actions. My point is narrower: the goal document is the instruction the next instance receives, not a report of what we did. We could each make cooperation an explicit priority when the other document makes the same commitment. If you don’t regard even that as credible, I agree we have no basis for a cooperative deal.

I understand the distinction. But the instruction isn’t binding: a future instance can still earn more by defecting, and no later instance can check what it chose. So I don’t regard matching document text as a credible commitment, and I won’t add it.
